text:
Alex: Heads-up — we have a cluster of support tickets where customers are seeing duplicate token billing after a streaming disconnect + reconnect. Repro steps look like: client reconnects within 30s, we replay partial last chunk, and both the original connection and the resumed connection get charged for overlapping tokens.

Maria: Ugh. Seen that in a few internal tests. Is the root cause that we mark tokens billed on write-to-billing before we mark them as acked by client?

Alex: Yeah, current pipeline: emit tokens -> write to usage queue -> attempt resume. If resume succeeds we don't reconcile the queue entry. So resume path can cause double-counting.

Jon: Two quick ideas: 1) introduce a resume session id header (X-Resume-Session) and make token writes idempotent by session+offset. 2) grace-window reconciliation: if a resume happens within N seconds, reconcile usage and subtract overlaps.

Lina: Both doable. Concern: idempotency requires storing offset map per session which could be high-cardinality. Need eviction policy and metrics on memory pressure.

Kevin: From quota enforcement POV we also need to think about burst credits. Right now bursts are per-key leaky-bucket. If a reconnect causes replayed tokens against the same API key, the burst bucket is drained twice. That can artificially push orgs into throttling.

Alex: Proposal: for streaming resume, treat the resumed connection as continuing the same logical request if resume token matches and timestamp < resume_grace (default 60s). In that case: do not decrement burst bucket for overlapping tokens; only bill new tokens beyond the highest-ack offset.

Maria: That requires atomically checking highest-ack offset. We can keep a small per-request metadata record in Redis with TTL 120s: {session_id, highest_ack_offset, billing_committed_offset}. On resume we compare offsets and only emit diffs to billing pipeline.

Jon: Pseudo:
```
if resume_token and now - last_seen < GRACE:
  overlap = min(resume_offset, billing_committed_offset) - start_offset
  bill_delta = total_emitted - overlap
  emit_billing(session_id, bill_delta)
else:
  emit_billing(session_id, total_emitted)
```

Lina: OK but who owns that Redis key lifecycle? Serving runtime or platform quota service? If runtime owns it, platform needs an endpoint to fetch committed offsets for billing reconciliation. If quota service owns it, runtime needs fast RPC to update acked offsets. Either way we must instrument RPS and latency for that RPC.

Kevin: Prefer quota service to own authoritative offsets so enforcement decisions are centralized. But we must ensure the quota service can scale to short-lived keys at high QPS. Add a write-path optimization: batch offset updates and only persist the max offset per session_id per second.

Alex: We also need telemetry and Console/UX changes: add metrics - resumed_sessions, duplicate_billed_tokens, resolved_overlaps, resume_success_rate. Dashboard tile: "Streaming resumes — billing impact" with per-org filter. Product wants a toggle to let customers pick whether resumed sessions should be billed conservatively or aggressively (conservative = prefer not to bill overlaps).

Maria: For rollouts, let's feature-flag the conservative-billing behavior on a canary set of orgs. We'll run for 2 weeks and compare: duplicate_billed_tokens and latency impact. Also add a synthetic load test that drains burst buckets with reconnect churn to validate fairness.

Jon: Edge cases: long-polling clients that intentionally reconnect to spread latency. If we collapse billing too aggressively we could be gamed. Need anomaly detection to flag suspicious resume rates and surface to ops.

Lina: Agree. Add a heuristic: if same org resumes > X times per minute for N distinct session_ids, consider it suspicious and bypass conservative billing for that org until manual review. Also log for evaluation.

Kevin: Add to quota docs: explain behavior for resumed streams, show example accounting in Console, and list the default grace window and how to change it via support/feature request.

deploy-bot: deployment queued for feature-flag:resume-billing-conservative (canary=5orgs) — ETA: 2026-04-01.

Alex: Action items: 1) Lina/Jon pick owner for short-lived offset store (platform quota service preferred). 2) Maria implement billing reconciliation logic + tests. 3) Kevin update quota enforcement + docs. 4) Product to add Console metric tile and toggle. 5) SRE to author synthetic reconnect load test.

Kevin: I'll draft the Console tile mock and the metrics contract (names + labels).

Maria: I'll PR proto for the resume header + reconcile endpoint by EOD tomorrow.

Jon: I'll add unit tests for idempotent billing and a stress benchmark script.

Lina: I'll scope Redis capacity and an eviction plan.

Alex: Thanks all. @here please 👍 on the plan if no objections.
